title: #Titans scrimmage notes 8-7-2026 (4) -1st play 2nd half Ward to Ridley for 1st down -Jeffery Simmons w/the pressure. Timed the snap perfectly and got in there to sack Trubisky -Khalen Saunders got in and chased Levis down for the sack -Trubisky took a shot to Ayomanor on a go rte. Joshua Williams stopped it for the turnover on downs -Explosive run by Nicholas Singleton. Got to 2nd level and pulled away from the 1st defense. They called it down but that looked like a TD. Nobody touched him -Simmons w/quick pressure ans Marcus Harris off the edge combined for would be sack -Ward tried to hit Tate on outbreaking rte. Alontae Taylor swooped in for the PBU -Wan'Dale Robinson is noticeably open all the time. Excellent feel for finding windows in zone. He and Ward are on the same page -Slye missed again from 50 -Mitch Trubisky to Dike for the TD in the back of the end zone. Dike went up and grabbed it over Kendall Brooks -Joey Slye tied it with a 40 yd FG -Offense got one play to break the tie from the 2 yd line. Marcus Harris came on blitz off the edge to knock it down. Defense wins

He's clearly itching to get back. Harbaugh, like previous coaches, raved about Nabers' football IQ.

title: Cool moment at the end of practice. The starting offense drove the length of the field against the starting defense. It was a marathon 13-play drive that reached the defense's 3-yard line after a big gain on a fourth-down checkdown to Dante Miller. The coaches tried to pull the units off the field because it had been such a long drive and they're planning to work on goal line tomorrow. But players lobbied for one more play and Harbaugh obliged. After a Dart timeout to sort out some confusion, he hit Darius Slayton running an out against Deonte Banks for a touchdown.

title: MUCH better today from Jaxson Dart and the Giants’ passing offense in one of the most grueling NFL practices I’ve ever seen Dart 🎯completed 16 of 19 passes, including 12 straight completions across 3 different periods at one point Unfortunately two offensive starters got banged up: 1. Center John Michael Schmitz looked like he got his bell rung early, left practice and didn’t return 2. RB Cam Skattebo limped off after Arvell Reese knocked him to the ground twice on consecutive runs and watched the rest of practice from the sideline 🔵The offense couldn’t run the ball, but Dart got the ball out quickly against the blitz when passing, even though he was sacked a few times. He completed 7 of 8 on a final drive against mostly 1s on defense and finished the drive with a touch TD pass to Darius Slayton 🔵Fantasy football update: Isaiah Likely is Dart’s favorite target, including an early deep fade to him over Deonte Banks 🔵Malik Nabers looked VERY good today running routes during individuals (see video) 🔵 Jason Pinnock replaced Tyler Nubin mostly as a first team safety. Nubin played with the 2s and rotated in with the 1s at times 🔵Although Harbaugh tends to rotate receivers around, it caught my attention that Slayton logged a couple reps with the 3s at one point 🔵3rd string LB Zaire Barnes had a pick 6 of QB Brandon Allen 🔵Jameis Winston was slinging it again. 19 of 20 by my count 👀
summary:
MUCH better today from Jaxson Dart and the Giants’ passing offense in one of the most grueling NFL practices I’ve ever seen

Dart 🎯completed 16 of 19 passes, including 12 straight completions across 3 different periods at one point

Unfortunately two offensive starters got banged up:

1.  Center John Michael Schmitz looked like he got his bell rung early, left practice and didn’t return

2. RB Cam Skattebo limped off after Arvell Reese knocked him to the ground twice on consecutive runs and watched the rest of practice from the sideline

🔵The offense couldn’t run the ball, but Dart got the ball out quickly against the blitz when passing, even though he was sacked a few times. He completed 7 of 8 on a final drive against mostly 1s on defense and finished the drive with a touch TD pass to Darius Slayton 

🔵Fantasy football update: Isaiah Likely is Dart’s favorite target, including an early deep fade to him over Deonte Banks

🔵Malik Nabers looked VERY good today running routes during individuals (see video)

🔵 Jason Pinnock replaced Tyler Nubin mostly as a first team safety. Nubin played with the 2s and rotated in with the 1s at times 

🔵Although Harbaugh tends to rotate receivers around, it caught my attention that Slayton logged a couple reps with the 3s at one point

🔵3rd string LB Zaire Barnes had a pick 6 of QB Brandon Allen

🔵Jameis Winston was slinging it again. 19 of 20 by my count 👀

🔵Fantasy football update: Isaiah Likely is Dart’s favorite target, including an early deep fade to him over Deonte Banks

C John Michael Schmitz was slow to get up after a run play in an 11-on-11 period. He walked off the field very slowly with a trainer. We’ll see what Harbaugh says, but seemed like a potential concussion. Lucas Patrick replaced JMS and battled to finish practice. title: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb on @1053thefan talking about his drops: “I just gotta focus up. I’m always thinking about a big play. Naturally, it’s caught, it’s caught, it’s caught, it’s caught, right? But then it becomes so normal that you lose track of the fundamentals. It always brings me back to square one. Catch, tuck, then make your move. Catch, tuck, then make your move. Catch, tuck, then make your move. “Every single drop has been always taking my eyes off the ball when the ball arrived because I’m automatically thinking I caught it. It’s just a way of the game humbling me and bringing me back to square one.” Lamb on his practice mentality: “As many times as I’m targeted, the ball should never hit the ground, whether it’s PBU, whether it’s a drop, whether it’s a bad ball, regardless of what it is. Any time the ball is targeted to me, I consider it a catchable ball. I don’t care if the ball is out of bounds. I don’t care if it’s all the way inside.”

title: Bringing you all on the inside for a first-hand, behind-the-scenes look at some of the latest and greatest recovery options the Broncos are providing their players in their new $175 million state-of-the-art facility. This allows their players to recover as hard as they train. Too many athletes miss the boat on this and only recover when they have an injury or do minimal amount. As hard as you train, recovery harder!!! You’ve got to outwork the world in all areas and that includes how you take care of your body. Check these out… Cryo-room — Not a cryochamber but a whole room. Dry float tank — I’ve only been in ones where you are immersed in water, have never seen a “dry” version until today. The Ammortal Chamber — a high-end, futuristic biohacking pod that combines five core non-invasive wellness technologies into a single 25-minute, zero-gravity session designed to accelerate muscle recovery, reduce stress, and promote deep nervous system reset. This absolutely calmed down my nervous system so my body could heal itself. Hyperbaric chamber — I do this couple times a week back home to try to repair damage done to my brain and overall recovery. Makes a huge difference in how I bounce back each week. Other amenities: Did 25 minute sauna at 185 degrees, their water area of their hot and cold plunge pools is fantastic! They also have sleep pods for quick recovery naps and a ton more. I cannot thank Beau Lowery and his incredible player health and performance staff enough for helping me out and showing me all the bells and whistles #broncos #recovery #training #nfltrainingcamp
